body:
## Why

A simulated user is a coding agent, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode, with a chosen model, playing a user who plans a trip (#66). It works from a shell, so it can't use the web page. `npm run chat` doesn't help: it runs the coordinator itself, on the developer's machine, against the local database. A session on the live site has to go through the app's API, the way the browser does, so its data is in the live database and its traces are in the server's Phoenix project, `road-trip-agent` (systems design, section 10).

This issue adds a terminal client that does what the browser does. It runs no agent. It signs in, sends the user's messages, and prints the replies, the option cards, and the itinerary. It also sends a card's buttons the way a click does. A simulated session then goes through the same path as a real one. Two things in `npm run chat` would make a session unlike a real one, and the client avoids both:

- Each `npm run chat -- --resume` adds the resumed line to the next message (technical spec 5.2), so driving it one command per message would make every turn look like a resume. Through the API, the server keeps a session's app lines between messages, as it does for the browser.
- `npm run chat` prints the coordinator's thinking, tool calls, and tool replies. A real user sees only the reply.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 3 (sign-in), section 4 (the API and its Server-Sent Events), and section 6 (local development).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 7.5 (option cards).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 7.2 (the option card's IDs line).

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add `npm run live-chat`, in TypeScript under `src/`, next to `src/chat.ts`. It talks to the app only through its API, never the database or the coordinator. Reuse what's in `src/shared/`, such as `messageRequestSchema`, `chatEventSchema` and `src/shared/chat-event-parser.ts`, and `src/shared/itinerary.schema.ts`, so `npm run check` catches the client breaking when the API changes.
- Run one command per action, and exit when it's done. A simulated user's harness runs one shell command at a time, so a long-running prompt like `npm run chat`'s won't work. It has to:
  - start a trip with a first message (`POST /api/trips`), and print the new trip and session IDs.
  - send a message to a session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/messages`).
  - start a new session on a trip (`POST /api/trips/:tripId/sessions`), and open an old session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/resume`), as a user does who comes back another day.
  - print the itinerary, as the itinerary view shows it.
  - print the open option cards, with a number on each option.
  - send a card's buttons: Select on an option, More options, Higher tier, and Lower tier. Send the same message and the same option card IDs a click sends (`web/src/option-card.tsx`). Move the words of those messages into `src/shared/`, so the web page and the client can't drift apart.
- Read the message from standard input, so it can be more than one line, and needs no shell quoting.
- Print only what the web page shows: the reply text, and while a turn runs, the name of each tool the coordinator calls, as the chat's "waiting on" line shows it. Never the thinking, the tool inputs, or the tool replies. After each reply, say how many option cards are open, so the simulated user knows to look, as a web user sees a card appear.
- Sign in with Supabase's email and password sign-in, as `web/src/sign-in-page.tsx` does. The site's address, the email, and the password come from environment values, checked with Zod when the command starts. Never take the password as a command-line argument, since a harness shows each command it runs. The Supabase URL and publishable key are already in `.env` as `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
- The site's address can be the local stack, `http://localhost:5173` with `npm run dev`, or the live site, `https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`. Both use the same Supabase project, so the same user signs in to either (systems design, section 6).
- Add a `whoami` action that signs in and prints the user's ID and email, from Supabase's sign-in reply. #66 uses it to list each bot user's ID with its harness and model, with no Supabase admin key.
- Add the command to DEVELOPMENT.md section 2.
- A turn can take minutes when workers run. The longest in Phoenix so far took about 4 minutes. Wait for the turn's end event, with no timeout of the client's own.

## Done when

- Against the local stack, with a Supabase user made for testing: a short chat starts a trip, gets an option card, selects an option with the client, and asks for a higher tier with it. Each turn's trace is in the `road-trip-agent-local` Phoenix project, under that user's ID.
- The client's output for those turns shows only reply text, tool names, and the card count.
- No check runs against the live site. Its first real use is #67.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
